title: Add minibatch surgical rollback instrumentation and quality-latch CI adapter
author: Avery Lin
description: Context and motivation: In production smoke runs we observed intermittent, high-amplitude regressions driven by single minibatches whose context permutations or prompt orderings caused cascading metric failures across downstream cohorts. Existing cohort-level gates detected failures only after large numbers of samples were affected, which delayed automated rollbacks and generated noisy incident churn. This change introduces two related capabilities: 1) minibatch surgical rollback instrumentation — a lightweight probe that isolates the exact minibatch and checkpoint delta that triggered a regression and generates a minimal rollback patch; and 2) a quality-latch CI adapter — a CI-side companion that can soft-fail early, annotate PRs with actionable rollback candidates, and optionally trigger gated rollbacks with annealed thresholds during escalations. Design summary: - Minibatch surgical rollback: • Adds instrumentation around the eval runner to tag minibatches with a stable replay seed and context fingerprint. • When a regression is detected by an upstream gate, the instrumentation runs a binary-slicing routine across the minibatch sequence (log2 complexity heuristics + early termination) to find the smallest subsequence that reproduces the regression. • Produces a rollback patch (JSON) that lists: checkpoint id, recommended roll-to model, minimal failing minibatch indices, diff summary (weights/tokens affected), and confidence score. • Exposes metrics: eval.rollback_candidate_seen, eval.rollback_confirmed, eval.rollback_latency_ms, and an early_fail_rate histogram for alerting. - Quality-latch CI adapter: • A small adapter that plugs into the existing eval-harness CI reporter pipeline. It consumes rollback candidate payloads and decides whether to mark the PR as soft-failed or to annotate the PR with an inline rollback suggestion card. • Supports a configurable annealing policy: thresholds start permissive on draft PRs and tighten during release branches or on flagged regressions. • Integrates with Linear so that rollback candidates create draft tasks when auto-annotate is enabled. Implementation notes and files changed (high-level): - eval_harness/runner/minibatch_probe.py: new core probe logic and binary-slicing routine with replay-seed tagging (approx 480 lines, documented). - eval_harness/ci/quality_latch_adapter.py: adapter that translates rollback payloads into GitHub PR annotations and Linear drafts. - eval_harness/metrics/rollback_exporter.py: metrics + exporter hooks (Prometheus labels + JSON webhook). - tests/integration/test_minibatch_rollback.py: deterministic replay tests + synthetic noisy-minibatch fixtures. - ci/fixtures/rollback_payload_example.json: example payload used in CI annotation UI. - infra/alerting/rollback_rules.yaml: alert rules and dashboards snippets. Commits (summary): - a1f4c2d: initial probe scaffolding and seed tagging - b3d7f5e: implement binary-slicing search and early-terminate heuristics - c8e9aaf: exporter + metrics and unit tests - d4b2e55: quality-latch adapter + PR annotation plumbing - e6f1b21: integration tests, docs, and sample payloads Review checklist (what I validated locally): - Unit tests: minibatch probe unit coverage 92% - Integration smoke: synthetic regression reproduced and rollback candidate generated - Metrics: Prometheus exporter exposes expected labels - CI adapter: creates PR annotation with rollback card in staging GH org - Performance: probe overhead < 6% on typical smoke runs (measured on a 32-sample smoke batch) - Security: payloads sanitized before annotating PR Description of tests and CI behavior: - On first push: CI runs full eval-harness suite. The quality-latch adapter runs in soft-fail mode by default (does not block merge) and attaches annotations. - On release branches or when the annealing policy crosses a configured threshold, quality-latch flips to hard-fail and will block merging until either: a) rollback is applied, b) a manual override is recorded in Linear, or c) the gate is dismissed by two reviewers. - CI runs initially failed on one flaky integration test in tests/integration/test_minibatch_rollback.py (seed scheduling mismatch); fix was pushed in commit e6f1b21 and runs were re-triggered. Review conversation (high-level timeline): - Samir (reviewer): "Nice approach — binary-slicing looks promising. A couple of requests: make the slicing abort after 5 attempts if it doesn't narrow and add metrics for aborted runs." - Author (Avery): "Added early-terminate heuristics and prometheus metric eval.rollback_aborted in b3d7f5e and exported it in rollback_exporter.py." - Maya (reviewer): "Quality-latch adapter should not auto-create Linear tasks on forks; suggest gating via org-level flag." - Author: "Added org-level gating and a configurable allow_fork_auto_annotate flag. Default false for forks." - Leo (approver): "Tests and perf numbers look good. Recommend squashing and merging once docs are updated." CI summary: - build: pass - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests: pass (after fix) - lint: pass - smoke-eval: pass - deploy-staging: pass Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2024-11-13 by Maya Chen. Release notes (for changelog): "Add minibatch surgical rollback instrumentation and quality-latch CI adapter — enables fine-grained rollback candidate generation and PR annotations to accelerate regression remediation during eval runs. Provides metrics for early_fail_rate and rollback latency." Backwards compatibility and migration notes: "No breaking API changes. Teams that consume eval webhook payloads should accept the new rollback_candidate v1 schema; the adapter ships example payloads and a migration script in ci/fixtures. If teams rely on automatic Linear creation in orgs with forks enabled, they should explicitly opt-in via the allow_fork_auto_annotate flag. Follow-up work tracked in ENG-2001: make rollback candidate suggestions automatically apply to Canary lanes when canary-stable=true." Additional context: "This PR intentionally keeps the automatic remediation path opt-in. The surgical rollback is designed to reduce blast radius of false positives by offering minimal, reviewable rollback patches instead of immediate cluster-wide rollbacks. The quality-latch provides a flexible path for infra teams to adopt this behavior gradually."
